THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE  COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11401  MFA No. 23910 of 2013  ORAL JUDGMENT
This appeal is by injured/claimant seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by judgment and award dated 11.05.2021 passed in MVC No.247/2009 on the file of learned Addl.
Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Haveri1.

2. Learned counsel Sri. Girish S Hiremath for the appellant/injured submits that the Tribunal has committed a grave error in assessing the income of the injured at Rs.3,000/- per month, as the claimant was a vegetable vendor and earning more than Rs.10,000/- per month.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has further committed an error in assessing the disability of the injured at 7%, which is contrary to the oral testimony of PW7 and other medical evidence on record.
Thus, he seeks to reassess the same by allowing the appeal.
3. Though notice was served on respondent No.1/owner of the offending vehicle, he remained unrepresented and placed exparte.

4. Per contra, learned counsel S.C. Jainar for respondent No.2/Insurance Company supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that the 'Tribunal', for short NC:
2024:KHC-D:11401 present appeal is filed by the injured only seeking enhancement of compensation and there is no challenge to the liability as such, as the Tribunal has rightly saddled liability on the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, he submits that appropriate order may be passed, taking note of evidence available on record.
5. I have heard the arguments of learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record.
6. The pleadings and evidence on record indicate that on 29.06.2008, the appellant along with others was travelling in Mahindra Goods Vehicle bearing registration No.KA-27/9800 along with vegetables.
The said vehicle met with accident resulting in injuries to the appellant.
The evidence available on record further indicates that the appellant has failed to prove that he was travelling in the goods vehicle along with vegetables.

The Tribunal taking note of evidence available on record,
saddled the liability on the owner of the vehicle by holding that the appellant was travelling in the said vehicle as a gratuitous passenger.

The said finding is not under challenge in this appeal, hence,
question of liability cannot be gone into.

sentences.text: Insofar as entitlement of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed notional income of the injured at Rs.3,000/- per month.
Admittedly, the appellant has not placed on record any cogent and acceptable evidence with regard to her income.
Hence, this Court taking note of notional income chart prepared by KSLSA, would re-assess notional income of the injured at Rs.4,250/- per month.
The Tribunal taking note of oral testimony of PW7-Dr. Kantesh Bhimakkanavar and other medical evidence available on record has assessed disability of the injured at 7%, which is on the lower side.

Taking note of observation made by the Tribunal at paragraphs-27 and 28 and also taking note of injuries sustained by the appellant, I am of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to re-assess the disability of the appellant at 10%.

Thus, loss of future earnings due to disability is reckoned as under:
Rs.4,250 x 12 x 15 x 10/100 = Rs.76,500/-
8.
Taking note of treatment provided to the appellant and also duration of treatment taken by her in the hospital, the compensation is re

- assessed as under:
 Pain and suffering Rs.40,000/-
 Loss of amenities Rs.25,000/-
 Loss of earning during laid-up period Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of future earnings due to disability Rs.76,500/-

NC: 2024:KHC-D:11401 Medical expenses Rs. 5,000/-
Food, diet, nourishment & attendant Rs.10,000/-

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands partly allowed.

b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the appellant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,71,500/- as against Rs.66,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
